hints: Look at the word all in the question, then ask yourself which of these four structures is found in every single bacterium and which is only found in some.
Remember the big prokaryote rule: they always have a boundary and wall for support, but they never have membrane-bound organelles like ER.
walkthrough:
**Recall what every prokaryote must have**

Think of a bacterial cell like a simple bag. It must have a cell surface membrane to control entry and exit, and it must have a cell wall outside for strength and shape.

These two are universal in prokaryotes.

**Recall what no prokaryote can have**

Prokaryotic means before nucleus, so no membrane-bound organelles. The endoplasmic reticulum is a large membrane system, so it is never present in a prokaryote.

**Check the flagellum**

A flagellum is useful for swimming, but many bacteria live attached or non-motile and never make one. So it is present in some, not all, prokaryotic cells.

Only membrane present, wall present, ER absent, flagellum absent matches row B.

options.A: Correct about membrane, wall and no ER, but wrong to say flagellum is in all cells, as only some motile prokaryotes have one.
options.B: Exactly right. All prokaryotes have a cell surface membrane and cell wall, have no endoplasmic reticulum, and do not all have a flagellum.
options.C: Wrong on two counts. It says cell wall is absent when all prokaryotes have one, and ER is present when no prokaryote has one.
options.D: Wrong on three counts. All prokaryotes have a membrane, have no ER, and do not all have a flagellum.
